newsitem.title: JAPAN: Street Fighters join Power Rangers in Sega merger.
newsitem.headline: Street Fighters join Power Rangers in Sega merger.

text.p: The merger announced on Thursday between Japanese toymaker Bandai and videogame maker Sega brings under one roof some of the most popular children's characters and digital games of the 1980s and 1990s.

When the merger takes effect this fall, Bandai's Power Rangers and Sega's Street Fighters will team up to take on rivals in the lucrative worlds of amusement arcades, toy stores and television channels.
Behind them march a host of other characters and videogames known the world over.
They include Sega's popular line of Grand Prix-like motor racing games and Bandai's Dragon Ball toy characters and Barbie doll challenger Sailor Moon.
Sailor Moon, The Mighty Morphin Power Rangers and Dragon Ball characters were all developed from Japanese television series, a source likely to remain important for the merged company.
Sega's videogames are on display in nearly every amusement arcade and are a popular travelling companion for adults and children.
Bandai also brings to the merger its "Virtual Pet", one of the cutest and hottest new products in Japan in the past few months.

Bandai began selling "tamagocchi", an electronic bird-like creature the size of an egg, last November 23. The digital pet can be fed and stroked and goes to the bathroom, just like a live pet, and will die if neglected.

With the "pet" already sold out in stores, Bandai said on Thursday it was stepping up production and expects to have total "tamagocchi" sales of nearly $100 million in the next fiscal year starting from April.
